lines.en: [Exclusive skill, ‘Fourth Wall’, activates strongly!]
The moment ‘Secretive Plotter’ stared at me, [Fourth Wall] stirred.
[Fourth Wall], growling like a wild beast protecting its young.
「Be care ful Kim Dok ja」

When I first came here, ‘Secretive Plotter’ had called [Fourth Wall] the ‘Final Wall’. The original novel had never given any information about that, but it wasn't as though I had no guesses at all. There were several kinds of walls in ‘Ways of Survival’, including Jang Hayoung's ‘Unidentifiable Wall’.
“I've come to receive my rewards, Secretive Plotter.”
Despite my words, ‘Secretive Plotter’ gave no answer.
Tzzt, tzzzt……!
Sparks flew around ‘Secretive Plotter’. The pitch-black darkness filling their face in place of an expression was questioning me, as though angry.
【Demon King of Salvation, why did you make that choice?】
“Pardon?”
Asked like that out of nowhere, I had no way of knowing what it meant.
‘Secretive Plotter’ asked again.
【Why did you not want to return to the third round? That worldline wasn't even your round.】
“That world once saved me. That's all.”
【Had you left him alone, he could have found rest.】
“That isn't rest. ……Secretive Plotter, why did you send me to that worldline?”
Tzzzzzt……
The sparks around ‘Secretive Plotter’ grew fiercer.
As though their very existence had become unstable.
With a sigh, ‘Secretive Plotter’ spoke.
【Everything was part of a story whose course was already set…… You don't know what you have changed.】
The pure-white holes where eyes should have been were looking at me.
【I will give you the promised rewards.】
I nodded.
There were three rewards promised for this sub-scenario.
An item, a Story, and a skill obtainable in the 1863rd round.
【Which item will you take?】
“This coat.”
A little tense, I held out the white coat Han Sooyoung had given me. The eyes of ‘Secretive Plotter’ narrowed, light seeping from them.
As expected, deceiving an ‘Outer God’ seemed to have been too much to hope for.
‘Secretive Plotter’ had promised one item.
But there was at least one item inside this coat's inner pockets.
【……Very well. There is one less flower returning, after all. The total probability should be about the same.】
[You receive ‘Infinite Dimension Space Coat’ as your reward item.]
Fortunately, ‘Secretive Plotter’ turned a blind eye to Han Sooyoung's coat.
Next came the ‘Story’.
【Naturally, the Story you will take is ‘that one’?】
“That's right.”
The only Story I had obtained in the 1863rd round was the one Yoo Joonghyuk had given me, anyway.
In fact, acquiring that Story here would mean revising part of my planned course…… But it didn't matter.
What mattered was seeing the end of the story I had chosen.
[You have received your reward Story.]
[This Story will take effect normally after you return to your original worldline.]
The last reward was a ‘skill’.
【What will you do about the skill? You wouldn't have acquired any new ones.】
“I didn't acquire a skill, but…… Would it be possible to receive the reward in this form?”
I began explaining to ‘Secretive Plotter’.
After listening to me for a while, ‘Secretive Plotter’ nodded.
【It is possible.】
[You have received your reward skill.]
[This skill will take effect normally after you return to your original worldline.]
That was everything I needed to obtain.
Something unexpected happened just as I finished checking everything and was about to ask ‘Secretive Plotter’ to send me back to my worldline.
Tzzzzzzzt……!
Amid powerful sparks, someone was trying to break into this space from beyond it.
I recognized the kind of ‘Status’ I could feel from the other side. Apparently, the <Bureau> had discovered that ‘Secretive Plotter’ had orchestrated this affair.
In other words, the one trying to intrude was most likely one of the Bureau's great dokkaebis.
【Go, Demon King of Salvation.】
With a slight movement of ‘Secretive Plotter's’ fingertips, a swirling portal appeared beneath my feet.
I urgently asked ‘Secretive Plotter’ a question.
“Wait! How many years have passed in the worldline I'm returning to?”
At my words, ‘Secretive Plotter’ looked back at me.
【Some stories are read quickly, and some are read slowly.】
At the bleakness in that voice, I tried to speak. But the lower part of my face was already passing through the portal.
【Demon King of Salvation. Do you think a story from which you have vanished would be read quickly, or slowly?】
From somewhere, I heard what sounded like playful laughter.
The portal activated fully, and my vision soon warped beyond recognition.
【When we meet again, I hope you will have become the proper owner of that ‘wall’.】
Was it because this wasn't my first time crossing worldlines? Even in the portal's raging currents that tossed my mind about, I managed to remain more or less conscious.
[‘Fourth Wall’ is activating strongly!]
[‘Viceroy's Dimensional Door’ is setting space-time coordinates.]
The passing scenery of the <Star Stream>.
Among memories floating up like buoys, I thought only of what I needed to do.
[‘Viceroy's Dimensional Door’ is closing.]
When I came to with that message, I was lying on the floor.
A spacious room, with dim lamps hanging from the ceiling. I thought I could hear murmuring from somewhere.
……Where was I?
I didn't seem to be on Earth yet.
Why? Why had I suddenly come here?
[The <Star Stream> has detected your existence in the worldline!]
[The <Star Stream> has recognized your modifier again.]
[The <Star Stream> assigns you a constellation context.]
[The <Bureau> assesses your Status.]
I thought I understood what had happened.
Through the ‘Otherworld Pledge’, I had left the scenarios of my original worldline.
There was a price to pay to reenter my original scenario.
Tzzzzzt……
The messages continued to appear as every muscle in my body seemed to spasm.
[The Bureau has completed your assessment.]
[You are unsuited to returning to your original scenario.]
[The Bureau is reviewing scenarios appropriate to your level.]
[The review is complete.]
I sighed at the messages that followed.
……I had thought it might turn out this way.
No, in truth, it had been inevitable.
I had left the worldline where I originally lived and visited another world.
And although the categories differed, beings like me who strayed far from their original scenarios and came back were all given the same name.
[You have acquired a new Story!]
[You have acquired a new attribute!]
[You have gained the qualifications of a ‘returnee’.]
[A new scenario is being prepared for you.]
I had become a returnee.
As I slowly sat up, I saw several men and women talking around me.
They were all returnees like me.
“Hahaha, I can finally go back to Earth! It's been ten years!”
“It's been twenty years for yours truly.”
“Where did you go? From your clothes, I take it you're from Murim?”
“I came from ‘Gratus’. Ever heard of it?”
That was when someone waved at me.
“Oh, looks like you're the last one, friend.”
It was a man in black martial robes. He wore a mask, but something about his exposed eyes and expression looked familiar.
I gave him a brief greeting, and he spoke to me again.
“Where are you from, friend?”
“Earth.”
“No, that's not what I meant. Is there anyone here who isn't from Earth……? I was asking which planet you were transported to.”
The man, smiling as he spoke in an easygoing tone. Suddenly, I thought I knew who he was.
「Cheeks bulging plumply like bags of tricks. Narrow eyes suited to night vision, and eyebrows half gone, as though pecked away by a crow.」
I inwardly gave a hollow laugh.
To think it was already time for this man to appear……
“The place I visited was Earth too. Earth in another parallel dimension.”
“Hmm, is that so? What an unusual fellow you are.”
The man held out a hand to me as he spoke.
“Let me introduce myself first. My name is Wang Weirong. In the <Second Murim>, where I've been, I'm known by the alias ‘Flying Fox’.”
Flying Fox (飛天狐狸), Wang Weirong (王卫荣).
He was one of the people who would later become Yoo Joonghyuk's companions.
“My name is Kim Dokja. As for an alias…… Hmm…… Shall we say ‘Demon King of Salvation’?”
Several returnees listening nearby burst into laughter.
“Demon King of Salvation? Bwahahahaha……!”
“That's quite a grand title! You must have been to some third-rate fantasy world!”
Hands slapping my back. Most of the returnees were from Murim or medieval-style other worlds.
Flying Fox grinned and spoke.
“A fine alias, friend.”
“You're too kind.”
“But it seems you've already been issued ‘returnee clothing’.”
“Ah, yes.”
I looked down at the [Infinite Dimension Space Coat] I was wearing. I'd completely forgotten that these clothes had originally been made exclusively for returnees.
I remembered Myung Ilsang, the ‘Disaster of Questions’ I had once fought. He had probably been summoned to Earth through the same procedure.
Just then, dokkaebis appeared in the air and began distributing coats to the returnees. Several who had received theirs looked back and forth between their coats and mine, then protested.
“Hey, dokkaebi! That fellow's coat looks better than mine……!”
Of course it did. It would make no sense for a coat from as far along as Scenario 95 to be inferior to a standard-issue one.
I saw several dokkaebis spot me, start in surprise, and report something to their superiors.
Would Bihyung know I'd come back by now?
I wanted to see my companions on Earth soon.
How many years had passed?
I hoped everyone was doing well.
Having received his returnee coat, Flying Fox grinned broadly and spoke.
“Ahh, the clothes really make the man. What will you do first when you get back, friend?”
“I'm going to look for someone first.”
“Oh, have you got a sweetheart waiting for you?”
I smiled. Flying Fox continued.

“Once I get back, I'm going to live it up. I've gained all this power, after all. No more cowering before that jerk who used to throw his weight around! The hard times are over. Nothing but happiness from here!”
“……It won't all be pleasant. Earth will have changed a great deal too.”
“Now, now, friend. You're sounding defeatist already. After everything we went through in other worlds, what couldn't we do back on Earth?”
[Returnees, please give us your attention.]
When the commotion subsided, the intermediate dokkaebi responsible for the returnees spoke on behalf of the others.

[Your return to Earth will begin shortly. You will be assigned a ‘main scenario exclusively for returnees’, which you will carry out in your homeland. We hope you will think of it as a simple game and enjoy yourselves.]
“A returnee scenario? Tell us exactly what it is!”

[Please check the scenario window for details. Ah, for reference, this is a group scenario, so there will be a leader. The being with the highest Status among you will automatically be selected as leader. Please bear that in mind.]
“Naturally, the leader will be me!”
“That Murim fellow over there looks pretty strong……”
They seemed curious about who would be this group's ‘king’.
[Your return to Earth begins!]
With a dazzling flash of light, all ten returnees began teleporting at once.
My vision shimmered briefly. When I opened my eyes again, we had landed in the middle of a sprawling city.
Broken paving stones, with gaps patched here and there.
A skyline formed by buildings whose reconstruction had begun.
It was unmistakably Earth.
“Where are we? Those letters……”
“It's Korea! Korea!”
A returnee from the Korean Peninsula jumped about in excitement.
Recalling the information about the ‘returnee scenario’, I shouted.
“Wait. Everyone, calm down and gather here for a moment.”
The returnees were already beyond control.
Several impatient returnees grabbed passing civilians and asked them questions.
“Excuse me, where are we? And what year AD is it?”
I sighed.
[The ‘Returnee Trigger’ has been activated!]
“They asked the d-date! They're returnees!”
“Aaaagh! Returnees! Everyone, run!”
“Report it to the alliance! Hurry!”
At the word ‘returnees’, the whole street erupted. Crowds fleeing like an ebbing tide, and returnees with bewildered faces.
“What? Did I do something wrong?”
[A new main scenario has arrived!]
[Main Scenario #45 ― ‘Glorious Return (錦衣還鄕)’ begins!]
I saw my reflection in a building's glass wall.
With a burst of sparks, my appearance was changing.
The form of a monster, hideous to anyone who saw it, seething with tentacles and filth.
Though that wasn't what I actually looked like, outwardly I resembled a small Outer God.
I probably looked like that to everyone on Earth too.
Because to the people of Earth, every returnee was a disaster (災殃).
Earth's incarnations, approaching step by step with hostility in their eyes.
When I looked back, the dazed Flying Fox was parting his trembling lips.
“F-friend. What on earth is……”
“Didn't I tell you it wouldn't all be pleasant?”
[The summoning of the 163rd returnee group is complete!]
[You are the ‘King of the 163rd Returnee Group’.]
It was the first dream in a while.
Acrid smoke spreading through the hazy field of vision.
It was clearly Korea, but there were unfamiliar structures, Story Weapons never seen before, and a pitch-black sky like that of a world on the brink of destruction……
In the dream, Han Sooyoung muttered.
What the hell was this?
But no voice came out.
Krrrrang!
Two men were fighting before her. One in a black coat, the other in a white one. She had seen this scene before, but something was different. Because the two men had identical faces.
……Yoo Joonghyuk?
With a stabbing sound, the two Yoo Joonghyuks vanished before her eyes.
What on earth was happening? What on earth was she seeing?
Not far away, she could see Kim Dokja.
Kim Dokja, on his knees like a man who had lost everything. Just as Han Sooyoung reached out and approached, someone called to her from right beside her.
—That's far enough.
When she turned, there stood a ‘Han Sooyoung’ with the same face as hers. A chilling sensation ran up her spine. With a cold shock like a bucket of water thrown over her, Han Sooyoung jolted awake.
With a faint groan, she sprang upright. She had been lying on a sofa.
“……Another stupid dream? Damn it.”

It was a dream she had been having repeatedly for the past few days. Yoo Joonghyuk fighting Yoo Joonghyuk, while another version of herself and Kim Dokja watched. At first, she had wondered if it might be a prophetic dream. But however she tried to interpret it, she couldn't make sense of it.
News was playing on a television some distance away.
—The launch of a new incarnation alliance is causing a seismic shift in the situation on the Korean Peninsula……
Han Sooyoung got up in a daze and rolled the cold ice in her mouth around as she listened to the news.
……Huh? Ice?
“What's this? Did you put it in my mouth, ajumma?”
“Why would I do a thing like that?”
Lee Sookyung, who had set out water and was offering devout prayers, answered without even turning around.
Han Sooyoung frowned and crunched the ice. Then was it Yoo Sangah?
“How many hours was I asleep?”
“Two.”
“Where's Yoo Sangah?”
“To the break room for coffee.”
“What break room? Do you think this is still a company office?”
Despite her words, the office where they lived was in an abandoned company building. Grumbling, Han Sooyoung got up and headed for the break room.
“Hey, what are you doing?”

A small paper cup sat on the break room table. Yoo Sangah, moving her pale fingers through the air. Information appearing in holograms streamed straight into her retinas. Startled, Han Sooyoung shouted.
“……Are you crazy? Are you using your stigma again?”
“You'll seriously end up in an early grave like that. Don't you know what happens if you keep overusing such powerful stigmas……”
The stigma Yoo Sangah was using was <Olympus>'s 「Hermes' System」. <Olympus>'s big-data network, which gathered information from across the <Star Stream> to calculate the future.
“I have no choice. We have to avoid the worst-case scenario.”
“I keep telling you, I know a fair bit about the future too.”
“That alone isn't enough. There are too many variables.”
The stigma 「Hermes' System」 drastically shortened its user's lifespan.

Despite knowing this full well, Han Sooyoung couldn't dissuade Yoo Sangah, because her contribution to bringing the group as far as Scenario 45 had been enormous. Without the future variables she had calculated, they would have faced serious crises in Scenario 35 or Scenario 40.
Han Sooyoung bit her lip hard.
If only he had been here……
It had already been three years since Kim Dokja disappeared.
It had also been a long time since their hope that he would return had begun to fade.
Steam rose from the cooling coffee. Watching it, Yoo Sangah spoke.
“Sitting here after so long reminds me of when I worked at the company. Back then, I'd slip into the break room to hide like this whenever I had a spare moment.”
“……I wouldn't know. I've never worked at a company.”
“You certainly aren't suited to office life.”
As Yoo Sangah smiled, Han Sooyoung pouted.
“Come to think of it, you said you worked at the same company as Kim Dokja, right?”
“Yes.”
“Were you two close?”
At the offhand question, Yoo Sangah looked into Han Sooyoung's eyes. With a faint smile, she answered.
“We were comrades-in-arms back then too.”
—Disaster alert! Disaster alert!
At the blaring alarm, Han Sooyoung ran to the office.
Lee Sookyung, who had been waiting, was checking the affected area on the television.
“……Again? Where is it this time?”
“Busan, apparently.”
“Busan? That's too far. The kids over there will take care of it.”
Han Sooyoung answered curtly and watched the breaking-news footage.
Tentacled monsters on the screen were battling the incarnations.
Lee Sookyung sighed and asked.
“Sooyoung, are you still keeping in touch with the others?”
“Why would I contact people who say they don't like me? Anyway, ajumma, something seems to be appearing in your bowl.”
At those words, Lee Sookyung looked down at her Star Relic.
Han Sooyoung asked.
“What were you divining this time?”
Lee Sookyung gave no answer. Sensing something strange, Han Sooyoung raised her head. Lee Sookyung had frozen like a stone figure of a wife awaiting her husband's return, utterly dazed.
Only then did Han Sooyoung realize something.
Three years since Kim Dokja had disappeared.
After all, there was only one thing Lee Sookyung would have been divining.
After staring into the bowl for a long time, Han Sooyoung spoke.
“I'm going to Busan for a bit. And where's Yoo Joonghyuk right now?”
I checked the scenario window floating in the air.
<Main Scenario #45 ― Glorious Return (錦衣還鄕)>
Category: Main
Difficulty: ???

Clear Conditions: After a long journey, you have finally returned to your homeland. Make your existence known to the people of your homeland, and leave a sign of your return at a major stronghold. The people of your homeland will welcome you.
Time Limit: None
Reward: 200,000 coins, removal of Disaster Transformation (災殃化)
Failure: Death
●While this scenario is in progress, incarnations perceive returnees as monsters (魔物).
●While this scenario is in progress, incarnations cannot understand the language of returnees.
These clear conditions are fucking awful.
Were they trying to get a rise out of me?
[Your target stronghold is ‘Yeouido, Seoul’.]
[There are currently no strongholds nearby where you can leave a mark.]
I quietly took a deep breath.
Right. Perhaps this was a blessing in disguise.
If I had to carry out Scenario 45 anyway, perhaps it was better that I'd become a returnee.
Because this scenario was practice for ‘a certain place’ that would open later.
“Fuck! Why are they attacking us?!”
The returnees under attack from the incarnations grew angry.
Not every incarnation who had survived this long was powerful.
Some still had no constellation sponsors, and some had joined the scenarios late.
So not all of the incarnations' attacks posed a threat to the returnees.
“I really can't take this anymore. Hey, everyone, let's just wipe this place out and—”
“No.”
The returnees' expressions hardened at my intervention.
“Why? They attacked us first!”
“There's a reason for that.”
“What fucking reason? Look at their faces. They look ready to kill us on the spot.”
It certainly could look that way.
I was at a loss as to how to explain the situation.
[The dokkaebis disapprove of your presence.]
Originally, Scenario 45 developed into an all-out war between the returnees and the existing incarnations.
My group number was 163, so the 162 groups summoned before us were probably causing trouble all over Earth already.
The First War of Return (歸還戰爭).
In the original novel, the Korean Peninsula of the third round was reduced to ruins by this war.
That was only if things followed the original novel, of course.
“What? The disasters seem to be talking to each other.”
“Kill them all now! The Black Flames Demon Ruler (黑炎魔皇) said so. It's easier to kill them when their guard is down!”
“No, didn't you hear what the Moonlight Empress (月下賢帝) said? There might be disasters we can communicate with, so we should watch and be cautious……”
……Those nicknames sounded familiar.
Anyway, if the incarnations could afford to talk so casually, the incarnations of the Korean Peninsula were still holding their own.
That was when a returnee waiting for me to speak grabbed me by the collar.
“Get in my way and I'll kill you first. Move.”
“What if I refuse?”
The moment the returnee raised their ‘Status’ against me, I caught their wrist too.
[Demon King, ‘Demon King of Salvation’, reveals his ‘Status’.]
With a crunch of breaking bone, the returnee whose wrist I held began to turn deathly pale.
“Y-you, what are you……?!”
The terrified returnee's legs were trembling.
[A temporary channel has opened.]
[The constellations of the Korean Peninsula turn their attention to you!]
[Constellation, ‘Bald General of Justice’, has entered the channel!]
[Constellation, ‘Maritime War God’, feels a strange sense of déjà vu from you.]
I was glad to see those modifiers, but this wasn't the time for greetings.
I addressed the returnees.
[Shut up and put away your weapons. Then get over here beside me. I'll cut off the heads of any stragglers, so move it.]
I deliberately spoke more harshly than usual. Feeling the difference in Status through my True Voice, the returnees hurriedly gathered around me.
But the returnees weren't the only ones thrown into confusion.
“Holy shit! What's that monster?!”
“Report it! Hurry, report it to the alliance!”
The incarnations who had sensed my Status were fleeing in terror.
I thought that might be for the best.
Flying Fox asked.
“F-friend. Don't tell me you're our group's leader?”
When I nodded, the returnees cried out in dismay.
“My God, there was a constellation among us……”
There were ten returnees gathered nearby, including me.
Three from Murim, five from generic medieval worlds.
And two from other places.
I began speaking as I examined their faces one by one.
“I don't care where you've come from or why you've returned here.”
The returnees watched me anxiously.
“One thing is certain. If we fail this scenario, we all die.”
Several returnees who had only just opened the scenario window groaned.
“We won't see our beloved families or friends, or set foot in the hometowns we've missed. Until we die, the people of Earth will remember us only as ‘disasters’.”

Both the returnee who had picked a fight with me and those who had been deeply shocked seemed to come to their senses, one by one. Some were looking at their reflections in the glass of a damaged building.
“Don't tell me we were attacked because……”
“It isn't just our appearance. There were other returnees summoned before us.”
Some returnees came back because they missed their homes, but others returned to destroy them. They had threatened Earth's safety, and perhaps were still doing so even now. I urged them earnestly.
“You mustn't fight. That will only lead to ruin.”
“What if we tell them we don't intend to fight?”
“It's doubtful they'd believe us, but in practice, even conveying our intentions is difficult. Until the scenario ends, our language won't reach them properly.”
The returnees' faces darkened.
“……Do you have another plan?”
“Avoid fighting as much as possible, and make leaving a mark at the ‘target stronghold’ your top priority. Then we'll clear the scenario and stop being disasters.”
Fortunately, this group seemed willing to listen to reason.
And with Flying Fox here, if we were lucky, we could complete the scenario without any major clashes.
But as always with scenarios, things weren't going to be that easy.
“The alliance! The Busan Alliance is here!”

Amid the shouts, figures approached through the retreating crowd of incarnations. Suddenly, my hearing grew muffled, and I heard something like a distant ship's horn. The breeze from Haeundae carried a faint trace of salt.
[‘Fourth Wall’ trembles faintly.]
Twelve ships appearing beyond Haeundae's sandy shore.
Two people were leaping down from the bow of a ship.
“The Maritime Admiral is here!”
“It's the Insect King (蟲王)!”
It hits me anew how much time has passed.
Some things had changed, and some hadn't.
The girl with her cap pulled low still wore her distinctive zip-up hoodie, but she was no longer wearing a school-uniform skirt.
The boy with the collecting net still had his distinctive sharp eyes, but his features were more defined and he had grown much taller. At least he was no longer small enough to cling to my thigh.
“Want to do it, kid, or should I?”
“Let's flip a coin.”
I'd missed them.
I'd wanted to see them so badly.
That was what I wanted to say.
A coin glittered above the pure-white sand. I knew I should run now, but I couldn't move my feet.
[Demon King, ‘Demon King of Salvation’, looks at his companions.]
Perhaps I had been harboring hope.
That if it was them, of all people, they would recognize me.
Perhaps that was what I had wanted to believe.
[Your ‘indirect message’ is distorted by the scenario penalty.]
And the next moment, an indirect message appeared in the air.
[‘Ugly Squid’ provokes the incarnation ‘Lee Jihye’.]
Lee Jihye looked at me and spoke.
“I'm killing that squid, kid.”
In Lee Jihye's hand was the Duke of Loyalty and Warfare's sword. It wasn't the Twin Dragon Sword that the 1863rd-round Lee Jihye had possessed, but it still performed quite well.
She'd probably taken it from some museum……
“Shall we slice up some dried squid?”
I moved the flustered returnees behind me.
“Jihye. Stop! It's me!”
I shouted desperately, but of course my words couldn't get through.
From Lee Jihye's side, it probably looked as though I were shrieking and waving my tentacles about.
“Ugh, you disgusting squid bastard. Die!”
Lee Jihye charging, her chilling blade flashing.
……This was starting to feel like the 1863rd round.
Shhkk!
Lee Jihye's blade skimmed narrowly over my head. As the severed strands of hair flew, Lee Gilyoung egged her on.
“Do it properly, noona! Cut the big tentacles, not the little ones!”
“Shut up!”
Apparently, my hair looked like tentacles to them.
I knew they were acting like this because they didn't know it was me, but I couldn't help feeling hurt.
I warned the returnees again as they backed away tensely.
“Nobody attack! I'll take care of this!”
If anything was a comfort, it was that the returnees were listening to me.
Flying Fox added in a troubled voice.
“Just say the word, friend. I'll help whenever you need me.”
Flying Fox was a returnee who had been quite an accomplished master in <Second Murim>. If things became truly desperate, I could ask for his help.
I wondered how I could make Lee Jihye realize who I was.
“Squid slicing!”
In this scenario, my ‘spoken language’ couldn't reach Lee Jihye.
But human communication had never depended on spoken language alone.
“What the hell? Stop moving so weirdly, you bastard!”

Activating [Way of the Wind], I began writing on the ground with dazzling footwork. Lines stretched across the ground as I dodged Lee Jihye's sword. The returnees behind me exclaimed, apparently realizing what I intended.
To be honest, I wasn't sure whether this would work. The original novel hadn't gone into detail about the possibility of communicating like this.
The question was how long it would take Lee Jihye to realize what I meant.
“What? It's writing on the ground.”

Fortunately, the perceptive Lee Gilyoung grasped my intention first. Lee Jihye paused in her repeated slashing and looked down. There lay the words I had written with my dazzling footsteps. The handwriting was bad, but not illegible.
It's me, Kim Dokja.
That was the sentence I had written. But then.
[The characters you have written are distorted by the scenario penalty.]
……Even this was subject to the penalty?
It was [Fourth Wall] that read the distorted sentence for me instead of Lee Jihye.
「I am a cool sq uid」
[Character ‘Lee Jihye’ activates ‘Demon Slaying Lv.10’!]
Red ghostly flames flickered in Lee Jihye's eyes, and she began accelerating toward me.
Shhk, shhkk!
Her strikes were far faster than before, and it gradually became harder to dodge them.
I even tried taking off my coat and waving it in surrender, but all my efforts came to nothing because of the scenario penalty.
[‘Ugly Squid’ provokes the incarnation ‘Lee Jihye’.]
“Die!”
My head was beginning to hurt.
If these visual illusions (幻視) continued, nothing I did would get my intentions across.
……As expected, simply subduing her would be best.
But for some reason, I didn't want to.
Had something changed inside me during my trip to the 1863rd round?
「Then, something occurred to the cool squid.」
Ah, wait. Maybe that……?
I thought for a moment, then decided to go ahead and try it.
